payload.objective: Find the molecular mechanism that best explains the loss of function of STAT1-p.Arg274Trp (STAT1, UniProt P42224) and test it with one targeted computational test.
payload.question: For a pathogenic missense variant in an immune-deficiency gene, which molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function, and does a targeted computational test change the conclusion that the starting evidence suggested?

payload.statement: ClinVar classifies NM_007315.4(STAT1):c.820C>T (p.Arg274Trp) as Pathogenic (criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts; 2 of 4 stars; 10 submissions) for STAT1-related disorder, Immunodeficiency 31B, Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial diseases due to partial STAT1 deficiency.
payload.strength: criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts (2 of 4 stars)

payload.text: Reply refused: factual statement without a recorded source ID: "UniProt and the variant literature describe R274W as gain of function (impaired dephosphorylation), while ClinVar lists it as pathogenic for partial STAT1 defic". Reply with record IDs only, or cite the ID next to each fact.

payload.statement: UniProtKB natural variant VAR_065943 at residue 274 (R to W) is annotated gain of function, increasing phosphorylation in response to IFNG, IFNA and IL27 due to a loss of dephosphorylation; annotated as Immunodeficiency 31B and IMD31C.
UniProtKB annotates residue 274 natural variant as in IMD31C, gain of function, increasing STAT1 phosphorylation due to impaired nuclear dephosphorylation (PubMed 21727188, 23709754).
payload.strength: UniProtKB residue annotation, ECO:0000269 cited PMIDs 21727188 and 23709754

payload.statement: UniProtKB annotates residues 136-317 of STAT1 as a coiled-coil region, and residues 257-286 as a helix; residue 274 lies inside both.
payload.strength: ECO:0000269 for coiled coil (rank 3 of 3); helix ECO:0007829 combinatorial evidence

payload.statement: AlphaMissense gives p.Arg274Trp of P42224 a pathogenicity score of 0.5268, classed as ambiguous.
payload.strength: computational prediction, not validated for clinical use (0.5268, ambiguous)

payload.statement: The AlphaFold DB model of P42224 covers the full sequence with mean pLDDT 87.25.
Eight of 10 experimental PDB structures of P42224 observe residue 274, and none of the eight carries the R274W mutation; the reference residue is present in all eight.

A 2025 Front Immunol review of STAT1 gain-of-function disease describes DNA-binding-domain mutations as associated with poor outcomes and reports GOF mutations as causing immune dysregulation through increased phosphorylation.
ClinVar lists NM_007315.4(STAT1):c.821G>A (p.Arg274Gln) at the same residue as Pathogenic (criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts).
payload.strength: criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts (2 of 4 stars)

payload.statement: Dephosphorylation rates in STAT1 gain-of-function variants were found to be normal, with high total STAT1 levels driving raised pSTAT1; delayed dephosphorylation was proposed earlier as the mechanism.

Heterozygous STAT1 gain-of-function mutations in the coiled-coil domain were reported in patients with autosomal dominant chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, where the abstract states previously described heterozygous STAT1 alleles are loss-of-function.

The article characterises the CMC-associated gain-of-function substitution arginine-to-tryptophan in the STAT1 coiled-coil domain as a member of a distinct subset of disease-associated gain-of-function missense mutations, and states that the molecular basis of these mutations is largely unknown.
No retrieved source measures the direct structural consequence of R274W on the STAT1 coiled-coil, its contact partners, or its dephosphorylation access in vitro.
payload.why_it_matters: Choosing between a domain-interface change and a partner-interaction change needs a structural measurement that the literature does not yet provide.

payload.statement: The subject line calls R274W a loss-of-function variant, but UniProtKB annotates it as gain of function and the retrieved GOF literature supports that direction; no retrieved source supports loss of function.
payload.why_it_matters: The mechanism must explain increased phosphorylation, not reduced signalling; a loss-of-function premise would point to stability or catalytic mechanisms that the evidence does not support.

payload.statement: R274W, within the coiled-coil helix, removes a surface contact with a partner protein (homodimer partner or the phosphatase that normally dephosphorylates STAT1), so dephosphorylation is slowed and phosphorylated STAT1 persists (gain of function).
payload.would_refute: A structural-context test that places residue 274 outside every predicted protein-protein interface, together with a stability or structure result showing no local change at the site, would argue against a partner contact at 274.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: UniProtKB ties R274W to impaired dephosphorylation (E2, E3) and the coiled-coil is the known GOF hotspot (E12), but E10 shows GOF alleles can have normal dephosphorylation, so this is not settled.

payload.statement: R274W, within the coiled-coil helix, weakens an intramolecular contact between the coiled-coil and another domain of the same STAT1 chain, relieving autoinhibition and raising phosphorylated STAT1 (gain of function).
payload.would_refute: Evidence that residue 274 contacts no other domain of the chain in the AlphaFold model or experimental structures, and that the substitution leaves the coiled-coil geometry unchanged, would refute an intradomain contact mechanism.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: The coiled-coil spans residues 136-317 and the helix 257-286 contains 274 (E3, E4), which makes an intrachain contact plausible, but no retrieved source names a specific intrachain partner for 274.

payload.statement: R274W destabilises the helix at residue 274, reducing fold stability, which is the loss-of-function premise in the subject line and would be the opposite of the gain-of-function direction in UniProtKB.
payload.would_refute: A predicted stability change in the neutral range at residue 274, or a high-confidence local model at the site, would argue against destabilisation as the cause.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: The only support is the moderate AlphaMissense score 0.5268 (E5) and high model confidence (E6), which do not show destabilisation, and the gain-of-function direction in E2 and E11 argues against it.

payload.description: Tests whether residue 274 lies in a predicted pocket or predicted protein-protein interface on the AlphaFold model. Interface membership supports H1 (partner contact). Absence of an interface supports H2 or H3 over H1.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: If residue 274 sits in a predicted interface, H1 gains weight over H2 and H3; if it does not, H1 weakens and H2 becomes the favoured intrachain explanation.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: Listed as can_run now with ProtVar pocket and interface data answering for this residue and P2Rank running on the AlphaFold model, costing 2 tool calls and 0 compute seconds without approval.
controls: Rank control: the rank and probability of the pocket among all predicted pockets of the model.
Confidence control: mean pLDDT of the pocket residues.

payload.description: Predicts the FoldX folding free-energy change of R274W on the AlphaFold model. A destabilising value supports H3; a neutral value weakens H3 and leaves H1 and H2 open.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A neutral value would rule out the loss-of-function premise for H3, but would not separate H1 from H2, and a destabilising value would still fail to exclude a gain-of-function mechanism.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: Listed as can_run now with the FoldX state ok, costing 2 tool calls and 0 compute seconds without approval.
controls: Within-site comparison: the same predictor for the other substitutions reported at this residue.
Applicability control: the model confidence (pLDDT) at the residue, because FoldX on a low-confidence region is not interpretable.

payload.description: Checks whether residue 274 neighbours a non-solvent ligand in the four experimental structures that hold one. It tests only ligand_binding, which is not among the leading hypotheses.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: Ligand-binding is not a hypothesis in this record, so a result would hardly move the ranking; ligands in the structures are soluble analogues (E7 ligands ACE, OXE, AU) that do not bear on a protein-protein mechanism.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: Can run now with 4 eligible structures, costing 2 tool calls and 0 compute seconds without approval.
controls: Negative control: ligands in the same structures that never list the residue as a neighbour.
Selectivity control: number of distinct residues that neighbour the contacting ligand, so a contact is not an artefact of a large neighbour list.
Site-state control: structures in which the residue itself is mutated are reported separately.

payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A local contact change at 274 would support H1 or H2, while an identical local fold would weaken both, but structure predictors are not validated for single substitutions.

payload.description: Run structure_comparison (T4) on the reference and R274W constructs, which needs human approval and 120 compute seconds, to measure local RMSD and contact changes at residue 274. An intrachain contact change at 274 that is confirmed in the comparison would support H2; a near-identical local fold would weaken H2 and leave H3 as the remaining option. Confirmation of H2 would need an experimental measure of the coiled-coil and domain contact in the variant protein.
payload.why_now: T1 has narrowed the question to H2 versus H3, and T4 is the next test that reads the local contact geometry directly. It is more informative than the FoldX stability test alone, but ESM Atlas must be reachable before it can run.

per_hypothesis.why: Residue 274 lies in no predicted protein-protein interface (in_predicted_interface null), which is the refutation signal named for H1. It does sit in buried predicted pockets, but a pocket is not a partner contact.

T1 does not measure intrachain contacts, so it neither supports nor refutes H2. The residue is buried (buriedness 0.74 to 0.86 in ProtVar pockets), which is compatible with a packed intrachain environment, but no contact partner is named.
T1 does not measure stability, so H3 is untouched; the FoldX test T2 addresses it.

payload.uncertainty: The test uses one AlphaFold model (mean pLDDT 87.25, E6), so predicted interfaces and pockets are predictions, not measurements. The absence of a predicted interface does not prove there is no partner contact, and buried pockets do not identify the chemistry. T1 can weaken H1 but cannot assign a mechanism.

The buried pocket membership (buriedness 0.74 to 0.86) is compatible with H2. The decision is provisional, since T1 does not measure intrachain contacts.

payload.text:
## Question
Which molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function attributed to STAT1 p.Arg274Trp, and which single computational test discriminates between the candidates? The premise is contested: UniProtKB annotates this change as gain of function [E2][E3], and no retrieved source supports loss of function [G2].

## Evidence
ClinVar classifies R274W as Pathogenic for partial STAT1 deficiency, with no conflicting submissions [E1]. UniProtKB annotates the same change as gain of function, with increased phosphorylation from loss of dephosphorylation [E2], citing impaired nuclear dephosphorylation [E3]. Residue 274 lies inside the coiled-coil (136-317) and a helix (257-286) [E4]. AlphaMissense gives 0.5268, classed as ambiguous [E5], on a model with mean pLDDT 87.25 [E6]. Eight experimental structures observe residue 274, all with the reference residue [E7]. Another study found normal dephosphorylation in STAT1 gain-of-function variants with high total STAT1 [E10], which challenges a dephosphorylation-only explanation. A coiled-coil gain-of-function substitution at this site is reported with its molecular basis largely unknown [E12].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
H1 (protein_interaction, rank 1): a partner contact is lost, slowing dephosphorylation. H2 (domain_interface, rank 2): an intrachain contact is lost, relieving autoinhibition. H3 (stability_folding, rank 3): the helix destabilises, matching the subject-line premise [H1][H2][H3].

## Tests considered and the choice
Four tests were considered [T1][T2][T3][T4]. T1 (structural context) was chosen because it separates H1 from H2 at zero compute cost and needs no approval [T1]. The stability test T2 was rejected as it only addresses H3, and the ligand test T3 addresses a mechanism no hypothesis invokes. The structure comparison T4 is unavailable now, since the ESM provider did not respond and it needs approval.

## Result
Residue 274 lies in no predicted protein-protein interface on the AlphaFold model [T1]. It lies in P2Rank pocket 5 (rank 5 of 11) and in three ProtVar pockets with buriedness 0.74 to 0.86 [T1].

## Updated decision
The favoured hypothesis changed from H1 to H2 [T1]. H1 is weakened because no predicted partner interface contains residue 274 [T1]. H2 is favoured but not confirmed, because T1 does not measure intrachain contacts [T1]. H3 is unchanged [T1].

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
The result rests on one predicted model, so the absence of an interface is not proof of no contact [E6][T1]. No partner or intrachain contact is named in the retrieved sources [G1]. H3 is untested, and the loss-of-function premise conflicts with the gain-of-function annotations [G2][E2]. Validation requires measured contacts and dephosphorylation kinetics in the variant protein.

## Next experiment
Run the structure comparison T4 on reference and R274W constructs once approval is granted and ESM is reachable. A local contact change at 274 would support H2, while an identical local fold would weaken H2 and leave H3 for the FoldX test T2 [T4][T2].
